resale_co.name: Certificate of Compliance (C of C, also called the 'Smoke Certificate')
resale_co.issued_by: Town of Boonton Code Enforcement / Housing (Code Official)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least two weeks before closing to avoid a late fee (inspection packet says no less than 10 working days); inspections are Tuesdays 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM; a final certificate takes at least 3 working days after a clean inspection.
resale_co.valid_for: Temporary C of C: violations must be corrected within 30 days
requirements: Completed application and fee paid before an inspection is scheduled
Full interior and exterior property maintenance inspection, including room measurements for sleeping capacity
All open construction permits inspected and approved before the C of C is issued
Exterior: sidewalks, drainage, weeds, accessory structures, unlicensed vehicles, siding, roof, gutters, windows, doors
Interior: stairs, handrails and guards, bathroom venting, dryer exhaust, plumbing, heating, electrical (GFCI), means of egress, sanitation and pests
Smoke detectors (10-year sealed battery units), carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers
If violations remain, a Temporary C of C may be issued with the buyer's letter agreeing to correct them within 30 days

fees.label: Certificate of Compliance, residential detached single family (Housing page)
fees.quote: Residential detached single family $100 per dwelling unit

fees.label: Certificate of Compliance, two family or multi-family (Housing page)
fees.quote: Residential two (2) family or multi-family $100 for the first dwelling unit, plus $50 per additional dwelling unit

fees.label: Late fee, request fewer than 5 business days before the sale (Housing page; the application says fewer than 4)
fees.quote: For any requests received fewer than 5 business days prior to a change of occupancy or sale, a fee of $75.00 will be assessed.

fees.label: Additional re-inspections after the one included re-inspection (application form)
fees.quote: will be charged $100.00 per re-inspection visit

resale_co.how_to_apply: Submit the Certificate of Compliance Application - Residential (Forms, Permits & Applications page or the SDL Portal, choosing Boonton Town not Township) with the fee to Town Hall, 100 Washington Street, Boonton, NJ 07005. Payment by cash, check or credit card. The fee includes the first inspection and one re-inspection.

evidence.quote: All properties must be registered and inspected upon a change of ownership or tenancy.
A Certificate of Compliance will be issued for every unit sold or rented. This certificate is also referred to as a "Smoke Certificate" and is required when closing on real estate.
Inspections are conducted every Tuesday between the hours of 9:00 AM and 11:00 AM.
Applications for a Certificate of Compliance (COC) shall be submitted at least two (2) weeks prior to your anticipated closing or rental date to avoid a late fee.
For any requests received fewer than 4 business days prior to change of occupancy or sale, a fee of $75.00 will be assessed

No owner, agent, or any person shall rent or lease or sell or in any way deliver up for use, change of use or occupancy any business, building, dwelling unit, lodging unit, rooming unit, or boarding unit, until a Certificate of Compliance has been issued by the Code Official.
Applications must be submitted no less than ten (10) working days prior to the anticipated closing date.
A minimum of three working days is required to process a Final Certificate of Compliance.
will be charged $75.00 per re-inspection visit

resale_co.notes: This record is for the Town of Boonton (1401), not Boonton Township (1402). The pack's ordinance link (ecode360 BO1072) is the Township's code; the Town's code is ecode360 BO1912, which has no separate resale CO or smoke certificate fee (Section 130-12 lists only UFC registrations and permits). The Certificate of Compliance is run by Code Enforcement/Housing and doubles as the smoke certificate. Re-inspection fees differ: $100 on the application (Rev 3/7/2026) vs $75 in the inspection packet (Revised 2/26/25); the late fee cut-off is 5 business days on the web page vs 4 on the application. Contacts on the Housing page: Rafael Tactuk, Code Enforcement/Prop. Maint./Zoning, rtactuk@boonton.org, 973-402-9410 ext. 632 (non-residential); Matt Mondino, Annual Housing Inspector, mmondino@boonton.org, ext. 627. The inspection packet letter is signed by Patrick Laverty, Chief Code Enforcement/Zoning Officer. Rental registration, annual rental inspections and lead-safe rules are rental items, not sale items.

requirements: Smoke alarms per N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19; battery-operated units must be 10-year sealed battery units
Fire extinguishers (still listed in the inspection packet)

fire_cert.notes: The residential phone extensions listed on the Housing page for Certificates of Compliance (625 and 626) are the Fire Inspector's and Fire Official's extensions on the Fire Prevention page, so the fire bureau appears to do the residential inspections. The packet still lists fire extinguishers, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) removed from the sale certificate in February 2025; confirm. The pack's LEA name said 'Boonton Township'; the July 2026 registry lists both Boonton Town and Boonton Township as F.

other_items.label: Open construction permits
other_items.detail: All outstanding construction permits must be inspected and approved before the Certificate of Compliance is issued. Work done without permits needs a retro permit.

other_items.label: Sidewalks and exterior
other_items.detail: The inspection covers sidewalks, drainage, grass and weeds, accessory structures and the building exterior.

other_items.label: Temporary C of C buyer's certification
other_items.detail: If the seller does not fix all violations, the buyer signs a certification to correct them within 30 days of the Temporary C of C.
